parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime converts gender presentation into a legal discrepancy at borders, security screens, government facilities and especially schools. Existing X passports and partial litigation do not offset passport/visa M/F rules, fraud-refusal discretion, birth-sex facility mandates, custody conversion policies, immigration-custody abuse, and bans on minor care or name changes. Public support and one federal bias conviction are mitigating signals, but no documented visitor-facing protection or effective remedy prevents institutional harm. No execution is documented; risk is severe rather than capital, especially for adult-with-minor travel.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports/visas restricted to M/F assigned at birth; X marker eliminated. Document or record discrepancies can trigger additional evidence, refusal, and possible permanent fraud ineligibility. Reports of passports blocked or confiscated leave travellers stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; litigation and an identity-document FAQ exist, but no documented visitor-facing shield against marker review.
entry_documents.interaction: Border marker review can convert a travel discrepancy into visa denial or fraud investigation, increasing later detention, facility or document exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections adopted policies described as conversion therapy for trans inmates: hair cuts, HRT removal, psychiatric therapy. Immigration custody has forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse. State bans custody name changes.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime law can be used federally, but no documented custody remedy or effective oversight for detained trans visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border, facility or arrest encounters can lead into detention where birth-sex placement and abuse are documented; minors face further erasure.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with gender; state requires public-school facilities by birth and is tallied as enacting public facility bans. Government buildings can deny or remove.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No documented visitor accommodation; private settings may serve normally but cannot override government or state facility rules.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Document or security outing can become facility exclusion in schools, courts, parks or offices; mapped jurisdictions criminalise refusal to depart.

care_services.exposure: State bans youth gender care, leaves one specialist clinic, and has religious-refusal law without state gender-identity protection. National rules target under-18 reimbursement and criminalise teacher facilitation.
care_services.protection: Ordinary emergency care is not documented as excluded; national employment ruling and municipalities provide climate, not visitor care protection.
care_services.interaction: A minor emergency, school visit or clinic encounter can expose identity, risking denial, disclosure, ward concerns, or criminal suspicion.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Entry cable treats sex discrepancy as fraud risk; counterterrorism prioritises radical pro-transgender groups; DOJ memo invokes radical gender ideology. Court language and polls frame trans identity as deception or danger.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy says not to target mere disagreement; some orders are enjoined, but this does not protect travellers already screened or detained.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing gives officers discretion to treat outing as dishonesty, radicalism or fraud, escalating stops into detention, exclusion or prosecution.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minors face public-school facility bans, youth-care bans, proposed reimbursement bars, denied name changes, and criminalised teacher facilitation. Guardians can be suspected of facilitating transition.
minors_guardians.protection: Same-sex marriage recognition is general and not a child-facing protection; litigation pending but no documented minor travel shield.
minors_guardians.interaction: A family trip involving school, clinic, transport or police can trigger birth-sex rules, outing, care denial, or prosecution fears for parent or teacher.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Trans violence is modestly above general homicide, 6.6 versus 6.0 per 100k, not organised sweeps. State lacks gender-identity bias law and has religious refusal; local protections cover few municipalities.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute and a 2017 federal conviction for bias murder show some recourse; public opinion and a pride event indicate acceptance.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street harassment may lack local remedy, while a police report could itself expose status if detention follows.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Adult visitor enforcement of facility bans, criminal trespass scope, airport security conduct, and marker rules in this state remain undocumented; no effective visitor remedy has changed operative restrictions.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Ongoing litigation, advisories and FAQs may help; several orders are enjoined, but no documented timely traveller-facing relief exists.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Legal uncertainty makes risk date- and itinerary-dependent, especially for documents, schools, custody and minors.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similarity: state-imposed birth-sex facility rules, hostile custody and immigration abuse, and official threat framing. Difference: no presentation offence or documented routine arrests of adult visitors, so it is not quite routine-sweep imprisonment; still severe because discovery is engineered through borders, facilities and custody.

Below. 0.25-D has birth-sex facilities and security fraud stops but lacks federal passport marker elimination, immigration-custody sexual abuse, corrections conversion therapy, and minor-care prosecutions. This dossier adds entry refusal/fraud exposure and institutional abuse, so lower severity despite similar facility language.

Much lower. 0.35-D features widespread service discrimination with some complaint remedies, but no national document or facility universal exclusion, and no custody abuse. Core exposure here is state-imposed universal restrictions across borders, facilities and custody, with litigation but no effective traveller remedy.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime makes outing consequential by design: border rules, security screening, government buildings, schools and custody all enforce assigned-sex categories. Recourse is partial and mostly climate-based; courts and some public support do not cancel documented entry refusals, fraud discretion, facility bans, custody abuse, or minor-care restrictions. Adult travel is high-risk, and adult-with-minor travel is worse because school, health, custody and name-change rules converge.
